parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define the Young modulus of a material.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: State an expression, in terms of some or all of $L$, $A$, $E$ and $\rho$, for the resistance $R_0$ of the wire.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Show that the spring constant $k_0$ of the wire is given by $$k_0 = \frac{EA}{L}.$$

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: The wire is stretched, within the limit of proportionality, by a tensile force $F$. Assume that any changes in the cross-sectional area of the wire are negligible.
parts.text:
On Fig. 3.1, sketch the variation with $F$ of the resistance $R$ of the wire.

{{figure:figure_3_1.png}}

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
On Fig. 3.2, sketch the variation with $F$ of the spring constant $k$ of the wire.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
Copper has a resistivity of $1.8 \times 10^{-8} \Omega \text{m}$ and a Young modulus of $1.3 \times 10^{11} \text{Pa}$.

A copper wire of diameter $1.6 \text{mm}$ has a resistance of $0.034 \Omega$.
parts.text: Show that the length of the wire is $3.8 \text{m}$.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Use the equation in (b)(ii) to determine the spring constant of the wire.

stem: A wire has length $L$ and cross-sectional area $A$. The wire is made from a metal that has Young modulus $E$ and resistivity $\rho$.
